Kendall County, part of the Chicago metropolitan area, combines the charm of rural America with the benefits of a growing urban region.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

Tax lien certificates represent unpaid property taxes. When you purchase a tax lien certificate, you pay the delinquent taxes on a property, and in return, you receive interest on the amount paid. In Kendall County, this interest rate can be as high as 9% every six months, potentially reaching 54% over three years if the property owner doesn’t redeem the lien.

Example:

  • Investment: $1,000
  • Return in 6 months: $1,090
  • Return in 3 years: $1,540 (if not redeemed)

If the property owner fails to pay the taxes and redeem the lien, you may have the opportunity to acquire the property through a tax deed.

Important Details

Pro Tips

  • Prepare Early: Register at least ten working days before the sale.
  • Understand the Bidding: The lowest interest rate bid wins.
  • Keep Funds Ready: Taxes must be paid immediately after the sale with certified funds for first-time buyers.

Attractions and Economic Highlights in Kendall County

  • Popular Attractions: Parks, theatres, historic sites.
  • Transportation Infrastructure: Good road connectivity, rail services, and proximity to Chicago’s airports.
  • Economic Development: Growth in sectors like agriculture, technology, and manufacturing.
  • Community Appeal: Offers outdoor recreational activities, entertainment options, and eco-tourism opportunities.

FAQs

What is a tax lien certificate?

It’s a certificate representing unpaid property taxes. By purchasing it, you earn interest until the property owner redeems it.

How much can I earn?

In Kendall County, you can earn up to 54% over three years.

What happens if the property owner doesn’t redeem the lien?

You may acquire the property through a tax deed.

When and where is the auction held?

Every November at the County Office Building in Yorkville, IL.
